c1-gen-0057: Cain feared that anyone who found him would kill him. Let's read Genesis 4:15 together.
c1-gen-0058: People journeyed from the east, found a plain, and settled there. Let's read Genesis 11:2.
c2-gen-0004: Cain was angry, and the LORD warned him that sin was waiting for him. Let's hear the LORD's words in Genesis 4:6 and 7.
c2-gen-0005: The LORD asked Cain where Abel was, and Cain said he did not know. Let's read the rest in Genesis 4:9.
c2-gen-0006: The LORD told Cain the ground would no longer yield its strength to him. Let's look at Genesis 4:12.
c2-gen-0007: The builders dreamed of a city and a tower reaching into the heavens. Let's find out why in Genesis 11:4.
c2-gen-0008: The LORD said, "Let Us go down," and the builders' plans came to a stop. Let's read Genesis 11:7 and 9 together.
c2-gen-0009: Each brother brought the LORD an offering from his own work. Let's check Genesis 4:2 and 4:4 side by side.
c1-gen-0059: On the road toward Haran, Jacob lay down with a stone at his head and dreamed. Let's look at Genesis 28:12 together.
c1-gen-0060: Jacob wrestled all through the night, and then came a word about his name. Let's hear it in Genesis 32:28.
c2-gen-0010: Twins struggled inside Rebekah, so she went to ask the LORD why. Let's read His answer in Genesis 25:22 and 23.
c2-gen-0011: A hungry Esau said, "What is this birthright to me?" Let's see how Genesis 25:32 and 34 sum it up.
c2-gen-0012: Jacob came to his father pretending to be Esau, and Isaac reached out to feel his hands. Let's read Genesis 27:22 and 23.
c2-gen-0013: Jacob came toward Esau, bowing to the ground seven times. Let's check Genesis 33:3 and 4 together.
c2-gen-0014: Jacob slept with one of the stones of that place at his head. Let's see what the morning brought, in Genesis 28:11 and 18.
c2-gen-0015: As day broke, the Man said, "Let Me go," but Jacob held on. Let's open Genesis 32:26 and 29.
c1-exo-0017: Someone from the tribe of Judah, my kind of tribe, was called by name for the tabernacle work. Let's meet him in Exodus 31:2 and 3.
c1-exo-0018: God told Moses to have the people make Him a sanctuary. Let's hear His reason in Exodus 25:8.
c2-exo-0002: God asked Israel to bring Him an offering for the sanctuary. Let's open Exodus 25:2 together.
c2-exo-0003: Moses sent word through the camp to stop bringing offerings for the sanctuary. Let's see what led to that in Exodus 36:5 and 6.
c2-exo-0004: Building the tabernacle took many gifted hands, and the women artisans had their part. Let's read Exodus 35:25 and 26.
c2-exo-0005: The tabernacle was finished at last, yet Moses could not go into the tent of meeting. Let's turn to Exodus 40:34 and 35.
c2-exo-0006: From the tribe of Dan, God appointed a partner for the chief craftsman. Let's find his name in Exodus 31:6 and 35:34.
c2-exo-0007: All through Israel's journeys, the LORD kept watch over the tabernacle. Let's read Exodus 40:34 and 38 together.
c1-lev-0001: God told Israel not to take vengeance or bear a grudge. Let's read Leviticus 19:18 and hear what comes instead.
c1-lev-0002: The Feast of Tabernacles lasted seven whole days. Let's look at Leviticus 23:42 together.
c2-lev-0001: Aaron could not come inside the veil at just any time. Let's read the LORD's reason in Leviticus 16:2.
c2-lev-0002: At harvest, Israel was to leave the corners of the field and the stray grapes. Let's see who they were for, in Leviticus 19:9 and 10.
c2-lev-0003: God told His people not to curse the deaf, and He had more to say. Let's read the rest of Leviticus 19:14.
c2-lev-0004: When Israel came into the land and reaped its harvest, the priest had a job to do. Let's check Leviticus 23:10 and 11.
c2-lev-0005: Aaron laid both hands on the live goat and confessed Israel's sins over it. Let's follow that goat in Leviticus 16:21 and 22.
c2-lev-0006: Once a year, atonement was made for all Israel. Let's check the calendar in Leviticus 16:29 and 23:27.
c1-num-0001: In the Valley of Eshcol, the spies cut down something that took two men and a pole to carry! Let's read Numbers 13:23.
c1-num-0002: Most of the spies came back talking about giants. Let's hear how they saw themselves in Numbers 13:33.
c2-num-0002: Joshua and Caleb told the people not to fear those living in the land. Let's read their reason in Numbers 14:9.
c2-num-0003: Caleb stood apart from the crowd that rejected the LORD. Let's read what the LORD said about him in Numbers 14:24.
c2-num-0004: At Kadesh there was no water, and the people contended with Moses. Let's read the LORD's instructions in Numbers 20:8.
c2-num-0005: The people spoke against God and Moses, and then fiery serpents came among them. Let's dig into Numbers 21:5 and 7.
c2-num-0006: Water poured from the rock, yet the LORD had hard news for Moses and Aaron. Let's read Numbers 20:11 and 12.
c2-num-0007: First the LORD opened the donkey's mouth, and He wasn't finished yet. Read Numbers 22:28 and 31 with me.
c1-exo-0019: At Marah the water was too bitter to drink, and Moses cried out to the LORD. Let's read Exodus 15:23 and 25.
c1-exo-0020: God promised His hungry people meat at twilight. Let's go to Exodus 16:13 and see what showed up.
c2-exo-0008: The morning dew lifted, and something small and round lay on the ground. Let's hear the people in Exodus 16:14 and 15.
c2-exo-0009: Moses said to keep none of the bread until morning, but some did not listen. Let's read Exodus 16:19 and 20.
c2-exo-0010: At Rephidim the people quarreled over water and tested the LORD. Let's hear them in Exodus 17:7.
c2-exo-0011: After the battle with Amalek, Moses built an altar. Let's read Exodus 17:15 together.
c2-exo-0012: The sixth day was a special gathering day in the wilderness. Let's look closely at Exodus 16:22 and 29.
c2-exo-0013: When Moses held up his hand, Israel prevailed, but even mighty arms get tired. Let's read Exodus 17:11 and 12.
c1-deu-0001: Near the end of his days, Moses went up from the plains of Moab to see the promised land. Let's look at Deuteronomy 34:1 together.
c1-deu-0002: Before he died, Moses laid his hands on the one who would lead next. Let's read Deuteronomy 34:9.
c2-deu-0001: Moses reminded Israel of the covenant the LORD made at Horeb. Let's open Deuteronomy 5:2 and 3.
c2-deu-0002: God gave Israel a reason to keep the Sabbath, straight from their own story. Let's read Deuteronomy 5:15.
c2-deu-0003: Moses told parents to teach God's words to their children diligently. Let's read Deuteronomy 6:6 and 7 together.
c2-deu-0004: Moses said the commandment was not up in heaven and not beyond the sea. Let's turn to Deuteronomy 30:12, 13, and 14.
c2-deu-0005: Moses set two ways before Israel, with heaven and earth as witnesses. Let's read Deuteronomy 30:15 and 19.
c2-deu-0006: The same words describe how the LORD talked with Israel and how He knew Moses. Let's compare Deuteronomy 5:4 and 34:10.
c1-deu-0003: Moses' farewell speech starts with the trip from Horeb to Kadesh Barnea. Let's check Deuteronomy 1:2.
c1-deu-0004: Moses got Israel ready to cross the Jordan without him. Let's hear him in Deuteronomy 31:2.
c2-deu-0007: Moses looked back on how the LORD brought Israel through the wilderness. Let's read Deuteronomy 1:31.
c2-deu-0008: Forty years in the wilderness is a long, long time! Let's read Deuteronomy 8:4 together.
c2-deu-0009: Moses warned Israel not to boast that their own might had made them rich. Let's dig into Deuteronomy 8:17 and 18.
c2-deu-0010: Moses told Israel to love the stranger, just as God does. Let's read his reason in Deuteronomy 10:18 and 19.
c2-deu-0011: The LORD said that unbelieving generation would not see the good land. Let's read Deuteronomy 1:35 and 39.
c2-deu-0012: Moses spoke a promise to all Israel, then said it again to Joshua. Read Deuteronomy 31:6 and 8 with me.
c1-2ki-0001: Naaman was a great and honorable man in Syria, but he had leprosy. Let's read 2 Kings 5:1.
c1-2ki-0002: After crossing the Jordan, Elijah asked Elisha what he could do for him. Let's hear Elisha's request in 2 Kings 2:9.
c2-2ki-0001: The widow kept pouring her oil into the borrowed containers, one after another. Let's go to 2 Kings 4:6.
c2-2ki-0002: The woman of Shunem could tell Elisha was a holy man of God. Let's read her idea in 2 Kings 4:9 and 10.
c2-2ki-0003: Naaman stormed off because the cure seemed too simple. Let's hear his servants in 2 Kings 5:13.
c2-2ki-0004: The Syrian army surrounded the city, and Elisha's servant was afraid. Let's read 2 Kings 6:17.
c2-2ki-0005: Elijah struck the Jordan with his mantle, and later Elisha took up that same mantle. Let's look closely at 2 Kings 2:8 and 14.
c2-2ki-0006: Elisha told the king to feed the captured Syrians and send them home. Let's read what came next in 2 Kings 6:22 and 23.
c1-1ki-0015: Ahab son of Omri married Jezebel, daughter of the king of the Sidonians. Let's read 1 Kings 16:31.
c1-1ki-0016: Naboth's vineyard sat right next to Ahab's palace in Jezreel. Let's look at 1 Kings 21:2 together.
c2-1ki-0003: Ahab wanted Naboth's vineyard, and Naboth said no. Let's hear Naboth's words in 1 Kings 21:3.
c2-1ki-0004: Ahab went home sullen, lay on his bed, and turned his face away. Let's read 1 Kings 21:4.
c2-1ki-0005: Jezebel wrote letters in Ahab's name and sealed them with his seal. Let's follow those letters in 1 Kings 21:8.
c2-1ki-0006: The LORD sent Elijah to meet Ahab right in Naboth's vineyard. Let's open 1 Kings 21:20.
c2-1ki-0007: Two scoundrels were seated before Naboth to accuse him. Let's read 1 Kings 21:10 and 13.
c2-1ki-0008: Ahab tore his clothes, put on sackcloth, and fasted. Let's see how the LORD responded in 1 Kings 21:27 and 29.
c1-2ki-0003: King Hezekiah broke the bronze serpent in pieces because the people burned incense to it. Let's turn to 2 Kings 18:4.
c1-2ki-0004: Hezekiah was sick and near death, so he prayed. Let's read the LORD's answer in 2 Kings 20:6.
c2-2ki-0007: The Rabshakeh mocked Judah for relying on Egypt. Let's read 2 Kings 18:21.
c2-2ki-0008: The people on the wall heard every taunt and answered not a word. Let's check 2 Kings 18:36.
c2-2ki-0009: Hezekiah was offered a sign using the shadow on the sundial. Let's read 2 Kings 20:10 and 11.
c2-2ki-0010: Hezekiah turned his face to the wall and prayed, and the LORD heard him. Let's dig into 2 Kings 20:3 and 5.
c2-2ki-0011: The LORD told Hezekiah not to fear the Assyrian king's words. Let's follow Sennacherib in 2 Kings 19:6, 7, and 36.
c2-2ki-0012: Hezekiah spread the Assyrian letter out before the LORD in His house. Let's read his prayer in 2 Kings 19:14 and 19.
c1-1ki-0017: The prophet Ahijah tore his new garment into twelve pieces. Let's read 1 Kings 11:30 and 31.
c1-2ki-0005: After a three-year siege, Samaria was taken in Hoshea's ninth year. Read 2 Kings 17:6 with me.
c2-1ki-0009: The older advisers told Rehoboam to serve the people and speak good words to them. Let's read 1 Kings 12:7.
c2-1ki-0010: Rehoboam answered roughly and would not listen. Let's hear the people in 1 Kings 12:16.
c2-2ki-0013: Babylon's captain of the guard came to Jerusalem, and buildings burned. Let's go to 2 Kings 25:9.
c2-2ki-0014: Many in Jerusalem were carried away, but some of the poor of the land stayed behind. Let's read 2 Kings 25:12.
c2-1ki-0011: Jeroboam feared the people's hearts would turn back, so he made two calves of gold. Let's look closely at 1 Kings 12:27, 28, and 30.
c2-2ki-0015: The LORD warned Israel and Judah through all His prophets: "Turn from your evil ways." Let's read 2 Kings 17:13 and 14.
c1-job-0001: Job's story opens with a blameless and upright man. Let's look at Job 1:1 together.
c1-job-0002: When Job's friends heard about his troubles, they came to mourn with him and comfort him. Let's meet them in Job 2:11.
c2-job-0001: The LORD asked Satan, "Have you considered My servant Job?" Let's read Job 1:8 and 9.
c2-job-0002: Hard news kept coming, and Job tore his robe and shaved his head. Let's open Job 1:20.
c2-job-0003: For seven days and seven nights, Job's friends sat with him in silence. Let's read Job 2:13.
c2-job-0004: Job wished his words could be written down forever. Let's read Job 19:23 and 25 together.
c2-job-0005: The LORD answered Job out of the whirlwind. Let's hear Job's reply in Job 38:1 and 42:5.
c2-job-0006: The LORD sent Job's friends to him with an offering. Let's turn to Job 42:8 and 10.
c1-job-0003: After a long silence with his friends, Job finally spoke. Let's read Job 3:1.
c1-job-0004: The LORD questioned Job, and Job said, "What shall I answer You?" Let's check Job 40:3 and 4.
c2-job-0007: Job poured out his sorrow honestly in his first lament. Let's read Job 3:25 and 26.
c2-job-0008: In deep pain, Job said, "Though He slay me." Let's hear the rest in Job 13:15.
c2-job-0009: Job said his complaint was still bitter. Let's sit with him in Job 23:3.
c2-job-0010: The LORD pointed Job to the behemoth, made along with Job himself. Let's dig into Job 40:15.
c2-job-0011: Job looked forward, backward, left, and right, and could not see God. Let's read Job 23:8, 9, and 10.
c2-job-0012: The LORD asked if Job could draw out Leviathan with a hook. Read Job 41:1, 10, and 11 with me.
c1-isa-0002: Isaiah's account of seeing the Lord on a throne begins with a date. Let's read Isaiah 6:1.
c1-isa-0003: Above the throne stood seraphim, each with six wings. Let's hear them call out in Isaiah 6:2 and 3.
c2-isa-0001: Isaiah cried, "Woe is me," because he was a man of unclean lips. Let's go to Isaiah 6:5, 6, and 7.
c2-isa-0002: Isaiah heard the Lord ask, "Whom shall I send?" Let's read Isaiah 6:8 together.
c2-isa-0003: People are like grass and flowers that wither and fade. Let's read Isaiah 40:7 and 8.
c2-isa-0004: God tells His people, "Fear not, for I have redeemed you." Let's look closely at Isaiah 43:1 and 2.
c2-isa-0005: The Creator never faints or grows weary, even when young men stumble. Let's read Isaiah 40:28, 30, and 31.
c2-isa-0006: Rain and snow come down and make the earth bud. Let's look at Isaiah 55:10 and 11 together.
c1-isa-0004: The Lord Himself promised a sign: the virgin shall conceive and bear a Son. Let's read Isaiah 7:14.
c1-isa-0005: The LORD invited a king of Judah to ask for a sign, in the depth or in the height. Let's open Isaiah 7:10, 11, and 12.
c2-isa-0007: Some people walked in darkness and dwelt in the shadow of death. Let's read Isaiah 9:2.
c2-isa-0008: A Child is born, and the government will be upon His shoulder. Let's turn to Isaiah 9:6.
c2-isa-0009: Picture it: the wolf with the lamb, and the leopard lying down with the young goat! Let's read Isaiah 11:6.
c2-isa-0010: Isaiah describes how the Servant would grow up before the LORD. Let's check Isaiah 53:2.
c2-isa-0011: A Rod from the stem of Jesse, royal family talk, and this lion is listening. Let's read Isaiah 11:1 and 10.
c2-isa-0012: God's Servant would be exalted and very high, and He bore the sin of many. Let's dig into Isaiah 52:13 and 53:12.
c1-psa-0016: Trumpet, lute, harp, timbrel, and cymbals: Psalm 150 is loud with praise! Let's read Psalm 150:3 and 6.
c1-psa-0017: Psalm 122 is a song for worshipers going up to the house of the LORD. Read Psalm 122:6 with me.
c2-psa-0002: "Who may ascend into the hill of the LORD?" Let's read Psalm 24:3 and 4.
c2-psa-0003: Psalm 29 roars about the power of the LORD's voice, and I like a good roar. Let's go to Psalm 29:4 and 5.
c2-psa-0004: The writer says one day in God's courts is better than a thousand anywhere else. Let's read Psalm 84:10.
c2-psa-0005: "Oh come, let us worship and bow down." Let's read Psalm 95:6 and 7 together.
c2-psa-0006: The law of the LORD is perfect, converting the soul. Let's look closely at Psalm 19:7 and 10.
c2-psa-0007: "What is man that You are mindful of him?" Let's read Psalm 8:4 and 5.
c1-pro-0016: Proverbs tells the sluggard to go learn from one of God's creatures. Let's look at Proverbs 6:6 together.
c1-pro-0017: Borrowing and lending can change things between people. Let's read Proverbs 22:7.
c2-pro-0002: A small creature stores up its supplies and food. Let's open Proverbs 6:7 and 8.
c2-pro-0003: Proverbs puts a slack hand next to a different kind of hand. Let's read Proverbs 10:4.
c2-pro-0004: One person scatters freely; another holds back what he should give. Let's turn to Proverbs 11:24 and 25.
c2-pro-0005: Proverbs weighs a little with righteousness against something else. Let's read Proverbs 16:8.
c2-pro-0006: "A little sleep, a little slumber," and then two sons at harvest time. Let's check Proverbs 6:10, 6:11, and 10:5.
c2-pro-0007: Proverbs warns against trusting in wealth or gaining it dishonestly. Let's read Proverbs 11:28 and 13:11.
c1-mat-0031: A man sowed good seed in his field, but while men slept, trouble crept in. Let's dig into Matthew 13:24 and 25.
c1-mat-0032: Peter asked if forgiving seven times was enough. Let's hear Jesus in Matthew 18:21 and 22.
c2-mat-0001: The servants wanted to pull up the tares, but the owner said no. Let's read Matthew 13:29 and 30.
c2-mat-0002: A man found treasure hidden in a field and sold all he had to buy that field. Read Matthew 13:44 with me.
c2-mat-0003: One servant was forgiven ten thousand talents, and then he met a fellow servant. Let's read Matthew 18:24 and 28.
c2-mat-0004: Ten virgins took their lamps to meet the bridegroom. Let's go to Matthew 25:3 and 4.
c2-mat-0005: One servant gained five more talents, and another gained two more. Let's hear their lord in Matthew 25:21 and 23.
c2-luk-0002: Abraham told the rich man that a great gulf was fixed between them. Let's read Luke 16:26, 29, and 31.
c1-jhn-0029: Nicodemus, a Pharisee and a ruler of the Jews, came to talk with Jesus. Let's look closely at John 3:1 and 2.
c1-jhn-0030: Jesus was weary from His journey when He came to Sychar in Samaria. Let's read John 4:5 and 6.
c2-jhn-0002: Nicodemus called Jesus a teacher come from God. Let's hear how Jesus answered him in John 3:2 and 3.
c2-jhn-0003: The Samaritan woman was surprised that a Jew would ask her for a drink. Let's look at John 4:9 and 10 together.
c2-jhn-0004: The woman talked about worship on her people's mountain and in Jerusalem. Let's read John 4:23 and 24.
c2-jhn-0005: The woman went into the city and invited the men to come and see Jesus. Let's open John 4:28 and 29.
c2-jhn-0006: Light came into the world, but people loved darkness because their deeds were evil. Let's read John 3:19 and 21.
c2-jhn-0007: Many Samaritans believed because of the woman's word, and then they heard Jesus for themselves. Let's turn to John 4:39 and 42.
c1-mat-0033: Judas went to the chief priests and asked what they would give him. Let's read Matthew 26:14 and 15.
c1-mat-0034: Jesus came into Jerusalem, and the whole city asked, "Who is this?" Let's check Matthew 21:10 and 11.
c2-mat-0006: Jesus overturned the money changers' tables in the temple. Let's read Matthew 21:12 and 13.
c2-mat-0007: The chief priests and scribes were indignant at what they heard in the temple. Let's dig into Matthew 21:15 and 16.
c2-mat-0008: Judas came with a great multitude carrying swords and clubs. Let's read Matthew 26:47 and 48.
c2-mat-0009: A third time, Peter said, "I do not know the Man!" Read Matthew 26:74 and 75 with me.
c2-mat-0010: Jesus kept silent before the high priest and gave Pilate not one word. Let's read Matthew 26:63 and 27:14.
c2-mat-0011: Pilate's wife sent him a message, and later Pilate washed his hands before the crowd. Let's go to Matthew 27:19 and 24.
c1-luk-0035: On the day Jesus rose, two of His followers were walking to a village about seven miles away. Let's read Luke 24:13.
c1-jhn-0031: After those appearances behind shut doors, Jesus showed Himself to His disciples again. Let's look closely at John 21:1.
c2-luk-0003: The two disciples recognized Jesus at the table, and then He vanished. Let's read Luke 24:31 and 32.
c2-jhn-0008: Jesus said, "As the Father has sent Me, I also send you," and breathed on them. Let's look at John 20:21 and 22 together.
c2-jhn-0009: Eight days later, Jesus invited Thomas to look at His hands and side. Let's read John 20:27 and 28.
c2-act-0003: The disciples asked if this was the time to restore the kingdom to Israel. Let's open Acts 1:6 and 7.
c2-luk-0004: Before He was carried up, Jesus spoke to His disciples about power from on high. Let's read Luke 24:49, 52, and 53.
c2-jhn-0010: After breakfast, Jesus kept asking Peter whether he loved Him. Let's turn to John 21:15 and 17.
c1-act-0029: In the church at Antioch, the prophets and teachers were fasting and ministering to the Lord. Let's read Acts 13:2 and 3.
c1-act-0030: By the riverside in Philippi, Lydia from Thyatira listened to Paul's group. Let's check Acts 16:13 and 14.
c2-act-0004: John had been assisting Paul's party, then left them when they sailed from Paphos to Perga. Let's read Acts 13:5 and 13.
c2-act-0005: At Lystra a man who had never walked was healed, and the crowd started shouting. Let's dig into Acts 14:11 and 12.
c2-act-0006: Paul stood in the midst of the Areopagus and told the men of Athens about an altar he found. Let's read Acts 17:22 and 23.
c2-act-0007: In Corinth, Paul found Aquila and Priscilla, recently come from Italy. Read Acts 18:2 and 3 with me.
c2-act-0008: Demetrius the silversmith warned that his trade was in danger, and a crowd got loud. Let's read Acts 19:24, 27, and 34.
c2-act-0009: Paul reminded the Ephesian elders how his own hands had met his needs. Let's go to Acts 20:34 and 35.
c1-heb-0001: Hebrews 11 opens by telling us what faith is. Let's read Hebrews 11:1 together.
c1-heb-0002: One man was taken away by faith so that he did not see death. Let's read Hebrews 11:5.
c2-heb-0001: Our High Priest was tempted in all points as we are, yet without sin. Let's look closely at Hebrews 4:15 and 16.
c2-heb-0002: God called Abraham to go out to a place he would receive as an inheritance, and Abraham obeyed. Let's read Hebrews 11:8.
c2-heb-0003: When Moses was grown, he refused to be called the son of Pharaoh's daughter. Let's look at Hebrews 11:24 and 25 together.
c2-heb-0004: After cheering us on to run our race, Hebrews says, "Therefore strengthen." Let's read Hebrews 12:12 and 13.
c2-heb-0005: These people of faith called themselves strangers and pilgrims on the earth. Let's open Hebrews 11:13 and 16.
c2-heb-0006: A great cloud of witnesses surrounds us as we run the race set before us. Let's read Hebrews 12:1 and 2.
c1-rev-0001: John was on an island for the word of God and the testimony of Jesus Christ. Let's turn to Revelation 1:9.
c1-rev-0002: John fell at Jesus' feet as dead, and Jesus laid His right hand on him. Let's read Revelation 1:17.
c2-rev-0002: The church in Ephesus tested those who said they were apostles. Let's check Revelation 2:2.
c2-rev-0003: Jesus told the church in Smyrna not to fear what they were about to suffer. Let's read Revelation 2:10.
c2-rev-0004: To the one who overcomes in Pergamos, Jesus promised some of the hidden manna, and more. Let's dig into Revelation 2:17.
c2-rev-0005: The church in Philadelphia had a little strength, kept His word, and did not deny His name. Let's read Revelation 3:8.
c2-rev-0006: Jesus told Sardis, "You have a name that you are alive, but you are dead." Read Revelation 3:1 and 2 with me.
c2-rev-0007: Jesus said the church in Laodicea was neither cold nor hot. Let's read Revelation 3:15, 16, and 17.
c1-rev-0003: After the letters to the churches, John looked, and a voice like a trumpet said, "Come up here." Let's go to Revelation 4:1.
c1-rev-0004: John saw a throne set in heaven, and One sat on it. Let's read Revelation 4:2 and 3.
c2-rev-0008: The four living creatures do not rest from their song, day or night. Let's look closely at Revelation 4:8.
c2-rev-0009: The twenty-four elders fall down and cast their crowns before the throne. Let's read Revelation 4:10 and 11.
c2-rev-0010: The living creatures and the elders fell down, holding harps and golden bowls full of incense. Let's look at Revelation 5:8 together.
c2-rev-0011: One of the elders told John to stop weeping, so John looked. Let's read Revelation 5:6 and 7.
c2-rev-0012: John wept much because no one was found worthy to open the scroll. Let's open Revelation 5:4 and 9.
c2-rev-0013: Countless angels and every creature joined the praise. Let's read Revelation 5:12, 13, and 14.
c1-rev-0005: John watched the first heaven and the first earth pass away. Let's turn to Revelation 21:1.
c1-rev-0006: John saw the holy city coming down out of heaven from God, prepared as a bride for her husband. Let's read Revelation 21:2.
c2-rev-0014: A loud voice from heaven said the tabernacle of God is with men, and He will dwell with them. Let's check Revelation 21:3 and 4.
c2-rev-0015: He who sat on the throne said to John, "It is done!" Let's read Revelation 21:6.
c2-rev-0016: John took a good look around the holy city. Let's dig into Revelation 21:22.
c2-rev-0017: The tree of life stood on either side of the pure river, bearing a crop each month. Let's read Revelation 22:1 and 2.
c2-rev-0018: The city has no need of the sun or of the moon. Read Revelation 21:23 and 22:5 with me.
c2-rev-0019: The former order has passed away. Let's hear what He who sits on the throne says next, in Revelation 21:4 and 21:5.
